<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS5" title="In 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.5 </span>Robustness to classifier choice</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S5.SS6" title="In 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">5.6 </span>Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation</span></a></li>
</ol></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_section"><a href="#S6" title="In Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6 </span>Discussion</span></a>
<ol class="ltx_toclist ltx_toclist_section">

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level
classification of contrast-enhanced mammography</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Sara Antonijevic
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Department of Statistics, Texas A&amp;M University, College Station, TX
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Brani Vidakovic
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Department of Statistics, Texas A&amp;M University, College Station, TX
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">August 24, 2026</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Contrast-enhanced spectral mammography (CESM) acquires two images of each breast, a low-energy image and a recombined contrast image, but two questions central to building a classifier on them remain unsettled: whether the two image types carry comparable malignancy signal, and how a patient’s several images should be combined into a single decision. Both are hard to answer reliably, because most published CESM classifiers split cross-validation folds at the image level, letting images of the same patient fall in both training and test sets and inflating reported performance. We pair a masked complex non-decimated wavelet feature bank with an elastic-net logistic classifier, evaluated under repeated patient-grouped nested cross-validation with patient-cluster bootstrap inference on the CDD-CESM dataset (<math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}880" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,880</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}880</annotation></semantics></math> images, <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients); under this leakage-free evaluation the inflation from testing on previously seen patients is negligible. On normal-versus-malignant detection, the two acquisitions are statistically
indistinguishable in patient-level AUC under the proposed evaluation framework. Under single-image fusion the contrast image reaches a patient-level AUC of <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> CI <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.918" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.918</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.918</annotation></semantics></math>) and the low-energy image is statistically indistinguishable from it, yet the two encode malignancy through disjoint, interpretable channels: phase coherence on the low-energy image and magnitude distribution on the contrast image. The framework matches a pretrained ResNet-50 representation at the patient level,
but whereas the frozen deep representation is not directly interpretable at the level
of individual predictors, every predictor in the wavelet representation carries an
explicit physical meaning. The result is a transparent, leakage-free baseline against
which future CESM classifiers can be measured.</p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Keywords:</span> complex non-decimated wavelet transform,
masked feature extraction, patient-grouped cross-validation,
patient-cluster bootstrap, multi-image fusion, contrast-enhanced
spectral mammography.</p>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Breast cancer remains one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers and
a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sung et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Siegel et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, and early detection
through screening substantially improves prognosis. Digital
mammography is the screening standard but exhibits reduced
sensitivity in dense breast tissue <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Boyd et al., 2007</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mandelson et al., 2000</a>)</cite>, motivating the development of adjunct
imaging modalities that recover the signal lost to tissue
superposition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Contrast-Enhanced Spectral Mammography (CESM) is a dual-energy imaging modality that addresses the dense-tissue limitation by acquiring two paired exposures after intravenous administration of an iodinated contrast agent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fallenberg et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Patel et al., 2018</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sorin et al., 2018</a>)</cite>. The lower-energy
exposure, the dual-energy mammogram (DM), resembles a standard
mammogram and depicts overall breast anatomy; the higher-energy
exposure is sensitive to iodine accumulation, and weighted
subtraction of the two yields a recombined contrast mammogram (CM)
in which normal tissue is suppressed and regions of iodine uptake
stand out. Because malignant tumors develop leaky neovasculature
and take up contrast preferentially, the CM image highlights
cancers that are obscured by overlapping dense tissue on the DM
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khaled et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fallenberg et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jochelson and Lobbes, 2021</a>)</cite>. From a statistical standpoint, the
consequence of this acquisition design is that each patient
contributes multiple correlated images per examination (two image
types <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> two views <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> two breasts) and any classifier
operating on CESM must therefore confront within-patient correlation
in both its evaluation framework and its patient-level decision rule.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Existing computer-aided CESM classifiers fall into two broad
families. Deep-learning pipelines, typically convolutional neural
networks fine-tuned from ImageNet-pretrained backbones, report
strong image-level AUCs on CDD-CESM, frequently above <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.90</annotation></semantics></math>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Acosta-Jiménez et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Helal et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, but
produce representations from which no
per-feature physical interpretation is recoverable. Hand-crafted
radiomic pipelines using first- and second-order intensity
statistics, gray-level co-occurrence matrices, and shape descriptors
are more interpretable <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Losurdo et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Marino et al., 2020</a>)</cite> but typically require lesion-level
region-of-interest delineation, which is labor-intensive at scale
and tightly couples the resulting feature bank to the quality of the
delineation. Wavelet-based representations occupy an intermediate
position <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vidaković, 1999</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ramírez-Cobo and Vidaković, 2013</a>; <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jeon et al., 2014</a>)</cite>, and are the basis for the feature bank developed
in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">A second gap, orthogonal to the choice of feature representation,
concerns evaluation. Cross-validation schemes that split at the
image level allow correlated images from the same patient to appear
in both training and test folds, and the resulting performance
estimates are systematically biased upward
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rouzrokh et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Varoquaux and Cheplygina, 2022</a>)</cite>. The magnitude of this inflation is setting-dependent and can be large:
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yagis et al. (2021)</a></cite> reported that slice-level cross-validation
raised test-set accuracy by <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="29" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>29</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">29</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="55\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>55</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55\%</annotation></semantics></math> across four brain MRI datasets relative to subject-level cross-validation. That figure is a worst case from a different modality, in which a single subject contributes many near-identical slices, and it indicates how severe leakage can become rather than predicting its size for CESM; the actual magnitude for a given feature bank is an empirical question, which the patient-grouped design of this paper answers directly (Section <a href="#S5.SS1" title="5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>). CESM is nonetheless a clear instance of the underlying problem, because each patient contributes a median of eight correlated images in the dataset used here, and the issue arises whenever the unit of analysis (the image) is nested within a higher-level unit of inference (the patient). Several recent surveys document that image-level cross-validation remains common in
medical-imaging classification work despite the inflation it produces
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rouzrokh et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Varoquaux and Cheplygina, 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">This paper makes four contributions. First, we introduce a masked
complex non-decimated wavelet feature bank for multi-image medical
classification, a representation that retains both magnitude and
phase at every scale and restricts all summaries to a multi-scale
eroded anatomical support, eliminating background contamination at
the level of the feature definition rather than the classifier.
Second, we evaluate the feature bank under repeated patient-grouped
nested cross-validation with patient-cluster bootstrap confidence
intervals, providing, to our knowledge, the first patient-grouped leakage-free benchmark for a
wavelet feature family on the CDD-CESM dataset.
Third, we use the framework to answer three methodological questions
about CESM classification that the patient-grouped evaluation makes
tractable: which of the two acquired image types carries the
malignancy signal when the same feature bank is applied to each; how
the choice of patient-level fusion rule affects reported performance;
and whether the modality and fusion findings are sensitive to the
choice of classifier family. Fourth, we benchmark the interpretable
wavelet representation against a pretrained ResNet-50 frozen-feature
representation under identical patient-grouped folds, isolating the
contribution of the feature representation while holding classifier
and evaluation framework fixed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The remainder of the paper is organized as follows.
Section <a href="#S2" title="2 Data and patient-level structure ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> introduces the CDD-CESM dataset and its
patient-level structure; Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> develops the
masked complex NDWT feature representation; Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> describes the elastic-net classifier, the
patient-grouped evaluation framework, and the patient-cluster
bootstrap; Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> reports the empirical findings;
Section <a href="#S6" title="6 Discussion ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> positions the contribution in the
broader literature.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Data and patient-level structure</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">CDD-CESM cohort.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the public Categorized Digital Database for Low-Energy and Subtracted Contrast-Enhanced Spectral Mammography Images (CDD-CESM) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khaled et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khaled et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, hosted by The Cancer Imaging Archive, which comprises <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,006</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}006</annotation></semantics></math> images from <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="326" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>326</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">326</annotation></semantics></math> patients acquired on two different mammography units. The two units are not interchangeable sources of images:
different detectors, calibration, and image-processing chains impart device-specific characteristics to the pixel data, and if the patients imaged on one unit differ systematically from those imaged on the other in case mix or acquisition period, then device identity becomes correlated with the malignancy outcome. A classifier trained on the pooled set could then improve its apparent accuracy by learning to recognize the scanner rather than the disease, a between-scanner confound that would inflate performance estimates in the same way that patient-level leakage does, but at the level of the acquisition device. To eliminate this confound at the source, we restrict the analytic set to the primary device, so that every image in the study is acquired under the same imaging physics and any signal the classifier extracts must reflect tissue rather than scanner. This restriction gives <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}880" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,880</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}880</annotation></semantics></math> images from <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients: <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="620" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>620</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">620</annotation></semantics></math> normal, <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="624" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>624</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">624</annotation></semantics></math> benign, and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="636" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>636</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">636</annotation></semantics></math> malignant, split evenly across <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="940" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>940</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">940</annotation></semantics></math> DM (low-energy) and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="940" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>940</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">940</annotation></semantics></math> CM
(recombined contrast) images. Patients contribute between <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> images each, with a median of <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> (one DM and one CM image per view, per breast). Each image carries a radiologist-confirmed pathology label together with structured Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) metadata.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">CDD-CESM provides per-image pathology annotations. For <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="47" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>47</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">47</annotation></semantics></math> breasts (<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87</annotation></semantics></math> images) on the analytic device the annotation differed across the two acquisitions or the two views of the same breast. In every one of
these cases the disagreement took the same form: an image carried a normal annotation while another acquisition or view of the same breast carried a benign or malignant finding, and the normal reads fell
predominantly on the recombined contrast image (<math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="78" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>78</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">78</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>87</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87</annotation></semantics></math> images). This is the expected direction, since the spectral subtraction that produces the contrast image suppresses tissue that does not take
up iodine, so a finding that enhances weakly or not at all can appear unremarkable on the contrast image while remaining the established diagnosis for the breast. Because pathology is a breast-level property rather than an image-level one, these per-image disagreements reflect how a single underlying finding presents across acquisitions and views, not genuinely different diagnoses for the same tissue. We therefore harmonized the image labels to the most significant finding for each breast, ranking malignant over benign over normal, and applied the resulting breast-level label to both image types and both views. This ensures that every image of a given breast carries the same outcome label, so that the classifier is trained and evaluated against a consistent breast-level ground truth rather than against acquisition-dependent label noise.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Patient identifier and grouping variable.</h5>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each filename in CDD-CESM begins with a case identifier of the form <span id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">P100</span>, <span id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">P101</span>, and so on, corresponding to the patient from whom the images were acquired. We extract this identifier from the filename and use it as the patient-level grouping variable for all subsequent statistical operations. The identifier serves two distinct inferential roles: it is the partitioning unit for repeated nested cross-validation (Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>), where all images from a given
patient are assigned to the same outer fold so that no patient appears in both a training and a test partition, and it is the resampling unit for the patient-cluster bootstrap (Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Patient-cluster bootstrap ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>), where the bootstrap draws patients with replacement and retains every image contributed by each drawn patient. The grouping variable is the mechanism through which the inference framework restricts both bias (via the cross-validation partition) and variance attribution (via the
bootstrap unit) to the patient level; image-level operations on either, given that each patient contributes a median of <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> correlated images,
would conflate within-patient and between-patient variability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The harmonization of the previous section operates within a single breast: it gives every image of a breast that breast’s most significant label. It does not act across breasts, so a patient with disease in one
breast and a normal contralateral breast still carries two distinct breast-level labels; <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="184" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>184</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">184</annotation></semantics></math> of the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients are of this mixed-label kind. Each binary task therefore needs a rule for reducing a patient’s images to a single patient-level label, and that rule is the same for all four tasks. A task is named by two pathology classes; we keep only the images belonging to those two classes, drop the rest, and label a patient positive if any of her kept images belongs to the more severe class and negative otherwise. For normal-versus-malignant, for example, benign images are dropped and a patient is labeled <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{s}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{s}=1</annotation></semantics></math> if any of her remaining images is malignant and <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{s}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{s}=0</annotation></semantics></math> if they are all normal. One consequence of dropping the off-task class is worth stating: the <math id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="57" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>57</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">57</annotation></semantics></math> patients whose every image is benign have no normal or malignant image, so they do not enter the normal-versus-malignant task at all and are never scored as negatives. Subject to this class restriction, no patient is excluded on account of holding mixed labels across her two breasts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We use the any-positive rule rather than majority voting because it matches the clinical decision being modeled – detection of the positive class in at least one breast, consistent with the worst-finding basis of BI-RADS assessment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">American College of Radiology, 2013</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zonderland and Smithuis, 2014</a>)</cite> – and because majority voting can assign a negative label to a patient with a genuine unilateral positive finding whenever her negative images outnumber her positive ones.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Masked complex NDWT feature representation</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Tissue mask and multiscale erosion</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The masked complex non-decimated wavelet feature bank is constructed in two stages: a tissue mask that defines the anatomical support over which all features are computed, and a complex non-decimated wavelet decomposition whose coefficients are summarized inside that support.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> denote a mammogram, represented as an <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{1}\times m_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{1}\times m_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> matrix of gray-level intensities. The black background surrounding the imaged breast is not part of the anatomy and must be excluded from every feature computation, since otherwise spurious zero values
inflate counts, deflate means, and bias higher moments of the coefficient distributions. We therefore construct a binary tissue mask</p>
<table id="S3.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle M(i,k)=\begin{cases}1,&amp;\text{if pixel }(i,k)\text{ belongs to breast tissue},\\
0,&amp;\text{if pixel }(i,k)\text{ belongs to the outside background},\end{cases}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mtext>if pixel </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> belongs to breast tissue</mtext></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mtext>if pixel </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> belongs to the outside background</mtext></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle M(i,k)=\begin{cases}1,&amp;\text{if pixel }(i,k)\text{ belongs to breast tissue},\\
0,&amp;\text{if pixel }(i,k)\text{ belongs to the outside background},\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">obtained by estimating the background level from the image border, thresholding above this level, retaining the largest connected foreground component, filling interior holes, and applying mild morphological smoothing. The tissue support is</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega=\{(i,k):M(i,k)=1\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega=\{(i,k):M(i,k)=1\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">and every summary defined in the feature bank below is computed as an empirical average over <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> rather than over the full image grid. This is the statistical-domain restriction that makes the feature bank scale-aware: it ensures that masked log-energies, masked quantiles, and masked phase summaries reflect the distribution of wavelet coefficients on breast tissue alone, not on a mixture of tissue and background that depends on the per-image size of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega^{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>c</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega^{c}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A single image-domain mask, however, is not sufficient on its own. The wavelet detail coefficients at level <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> are computed from a filter whose impulse response spans a finite spatial extent, so a coefficient at <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i,k)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i,k)</annotation></semantics></math> depends on pixels of <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> within a neighborhood whose radius grows with <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>. Coefficients near the boundary of <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega</annotation></semantics></math> therefore mix contributions from breast tissue and from the background, and this cone-of-influence contamination
becomes worse at coarser scales. To control it, we erode <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> at each scale to produce a level-dependent mask <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{e}^{(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{e}^{(j)}</annotation></semantics></math> whose retained pixels are guaranteed to be far enough from the boundary that the level-<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> wavelet coefficients depend only on tissue values. Erosion is performed with a structuring element matched to
the support of the wavelet filter at level <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>; in our experiments we use <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=7</annotation></semantics></math> decomposition levels. The multiscale erosion is a deliberate design choice rather than a preprocessing convenience: without it, every coarse-scale feature would carry boundary-driven bias whose magnitude varies systematically with the size and shape
of the breast in each mammogram, confounding the scale-decay signatures that several of the feature families described below are constructed to capture.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Complex non-decimated wavelet transform</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The masked image is then decomposed using a two-dimensional complex non-decimated wavelet transform (NDWT). In the experiments reported below we use a complex-valued Daubechies filter with coefficients given in Supplement S2 and in the released
code. Circular boundary handling is used in the non-decimated convolution so that all
coefficient images remain on the original image grid. At each level <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\ldots,L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\ldots,L</annotation></semantics></math>, the transform produces three directional detail subbands and one approximation subband:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle D_{j}=HH_{j},\qquad H_{j}=HL_{j},\qquad V_{j}=LH_{j}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle D_{j}=HH_{j},\qquad H_{j}=HL_{j},\qquad V_{j}=LH_{j},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">corresponding to diagonal, horizontal, and vertical detail content, together with the final smooth image <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>. Two properties of this transform matter statistically for the feature bank that follows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, the transform is non-decimated: the output coefficient image at each level retains the full <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{1}\times m_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{1}\times m_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> resolution of the input, rather than being downsampled by a factor of two per axis at each successive level as in the classical (decimated) wavelet transform. Every coefficient image <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{j,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{j,s}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\{D,H,V\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>H</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\{D,H,V\}</annotation></semantics></math> therefore has
size <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{1}\times m_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{1}\times m_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, identical to that of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>. The level-eroded tissue mask <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{e}^{(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{e}^{(j)}</annotation></semantics></math> therefore applies pointwise to its coefficient image at every scale, without resampling or interpolation: the mask grid and the coefficient grid coincide at every level, so only the erosion radius changes with <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, not the sampling. This pointwise alignment is what makes the masking operation well-defined as a statistical restriction: a
masked decimated wavelet transform requires upsampling the mask to match each scale’s coefficient grid, which introduces interpolation artifacts and a per-scale ambiguity in which pixels belong to the support. The non-decimated representation avoids that ambiguity entirely.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Second, because the filter is complex-valued, each coefficient is itself a complex number. The magnitude <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|C_{j,s}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|C_{j,s}|</annotation></semantics></math> carries energy and shape information and is the analogue of the real-valued wavelet coefficient used in classical wavelet feature banks; the phase <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\arg C_{j,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arg C_{j,s}</annotation></semantics></math> carries information about local oriented structure — specifically, the alignment and coherence of edges, ridges, and other directional content
within each subband at each scale. Real-valued wavelet transforms discard the phase channel altogether, and so cannot represent phase-coherence statistics; the complex non-decimated transform makes phase available as a separate channel of the feature bank, on equal footing with magnitude.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For any coefficient image <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{j,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{j,s}</annotation></semantics></math>, the masked working vector is
restricted to the level-eroded tissue support</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{j}=\{(i,k):M_{e}^{(j)}(i,k)=1\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{j}=\{(i,k):M_{e}^{(j)}(i,k)=1\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">the set of pixels retained by the level-<math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> eroded mask of
Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Tissue mask and multiscale erosion ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, giving</p>
<table id="S3.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.E5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle x_{j,s}=\{C_{j,s}(i,k):(i,k)\in\Omega_{j}\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle x_{j,s}=\{C_{j,s}(i,k):(i,k)\in\Omega_{j}\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.3" class="ltx_p">with magnitudes <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{j,s}=|x_{j,s}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{j,s}=|x_{j,s}|</annotation></semantics></math> and phases
<math id="S3.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{j,s}=\arg(x_{j,s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{j,s}=\arg(x_{j,s})</annotation></semantics></math>. All energy descriptors use <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|x|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not
<math id="S3.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, since the coefficients are complex. The masked log-energy at
level <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> in subband <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{j,s}=\frac{1}{|\Omega_{j}|}\sum_{(i,k)\in\Omega_{j}}|C_{j,s}(i,k)|^{2},\qquad L_{j,s}=\log_{2}E_{j,s}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{j,s}=\frac{1}{|\Omega_{j}|}\sum_{(i,k)\in\Omega_{j}}|C_{j,s}(i,k)|^{2},\qquad L_{j,s}=\log_{2}E_{j,s},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.4" class="ltx_p">and analogous masked averages define all higher-order moments,
quantiles, and phase summaries used downstream. The key point is that every sum is taken over the level-appropriate eroded tissue support <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, never over the full image grid.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 3.2 Complex non-decimated wavelet transform ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> illustrates the construction described in Sections <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Tissue mask and multiscale erosion ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> and <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Complex non-decimated wavelet transform ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> on a representative mammogram: the original image <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, the tissue mask <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, and a representative eroded mask <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{e}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{e}</annotation></semantics></math> are shown on the left, and the
masked smooth and detail coefficient images <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,2,3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,2,3</annotation></semantics></math> are shown on the right. Because the transform is non-decimated, every coefficient image has the same spatial size as <math id="S3.SS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, so the mask applies pointwise at every scale. An analogous display on the Lena test image is provided in Supplement S1 to make the multi-scale subband organization more transparent on a familiar non-clinical example.</p>
</div>

<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Feature families</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">From the masked complex NDWT representation we extract <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">203</annotation></semantics></math> numeric features per image, organized into seven families summarized in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 3.3 Feature families ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The families together span the kinds of image content that a multiscale representation can summarize: the marginal distribution of energy across scales (log-energy), the shape and tail behavior of the coefficient magnitude distribution at each scale (magnitude distribution), the relative balance among the three directional subbands (anisotropy and dominance), the coherence of oriented structure that magnitude alone cannot see (phase and coherence), the cross-scale persistence of strong responses (persistence and cross-scale), the rate at which energy decays with scale (energy spectrum slopes), and the level-to-level energy differences that this decay produces (adjacent-scale log-energy differences). A complete feature codebook with exact mathematical definitions and the naming convention used in the released code is provided in Supplement S2.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S3.T1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 1</span>: </span><span id="S3.T1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Feature families extracted from the masked complex
non-decimated wavelet representation of each mammogram. All summaries
are computed over the level-eroded tissue support <math id="S3.T1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> of
Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Complex non-decimated wavelet transform ‣ 3 Masked complex NDWT feature representation ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>. See Supplement S2 for the full codebook.</span></figcaption>

(e.g. circular correlation between </span><math id="S3.T1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\arg H_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">H</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arg H_{j}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.T1.5.5.2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> and </span><math id="S3.T1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\arg V_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">V</mi><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arg V_{j}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.T1.5.5.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">).
Available only because the transform is complex-valued.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T1.5.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S3.T1.5.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top">
<span id="S3.T1.5.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:93.2pt;">
<span id="S3.T1.5.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.T1.5.6.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Persistence / cross-scale</span></span>

and level-of-maximum summaries.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>

level </span><math id="S3.T1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.T1.5.7.2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> over selected ranges, capturing how energy decays with
scale.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T1.5.8" class="ltx_tr">

<span id="S3.T1.5.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:93.2pt;">
<span id="S3.T1.5.8.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.T1.5.8.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Adjacent-scale log-energy differences</span></span>
