<td id="S3.T1.5.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb">
<span id="S3.T1.5.8.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:227.7pt;">
<span id="S3.T1.5.8.2.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.T1.5.8.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Differences of the form </span><math id="S3.T1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{j+1,s}-L_{j,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">L</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi></mrow></msub><mo mathsize="0.900em">−</mo><msub><mi mathsize="0.900em">L</mi><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em">j</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">,</mo><mi mathsize="0.900em">s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{j+1,s}-L_{j,s}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.T1.5.8.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">.</span></span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Several of these families have direct radiological correspondences that motivate the feature-selection patterns reported in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>. Phase coherence indexes the consistency of local oriented structure and is therefore sensitive to architectural distortion and spiculation, which are the dominant low-energy mammographic cues for malignancy in the BI-RADS
lexicon <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">American College of Radiology, 2013</a>)</cite>. Magnitude-distribution descriptors index how concentrated wavelet energy is in a small fraction of the tissue support; on the recombined contrast image, where the spectral subtraction has already suppressed background tissue, this concentration corresponds to localized iodine uptake from tumor
neovasculature. Energy-spectrum slopes and adjacent-scale
differences describe the rate at which tissue texture coarsens with scale, summarizing the scale-invariance properties of breast parenchyma that are clinically reported as breast density. Anisotropy and persistence descriptors capture, respectively, the directional organization of tissue and the multi-scale support of
localized structures such as masses, distinguishing them from isotropic background parenchyma and from scale-specific noise. The correspondences motivate the feature-selection analysis in Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Modeling and inference framework</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With each mammogram now represented as a fixed-length vector of
masked multiscale descriptors, we turn to the predictive model that maps these features to a probability of malignancy, the
cross-validation framework used to evaluate it, the rules used to aggregate image-level predictions into patient-level predictions, and the bootstrap procedure used for inference on the resulting patient-level AUCs.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Elastic-net classifier and nonlinear comparators</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each binary task we model the class probability with a
regularized logistic regression. Let <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the image-level outcome and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math> the corresponding feature vector extracted from the masked complex NDWT representation. The classifier estimates the conditional class probability</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(Y_{i}=1\mid x_{i})\;=\;\frac{1}{1+\exp\bigl\{-(\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta)\bigr\}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(Y_{i}=1\mid x_{i})\;=\;\frac{1}{1+\exp\bigl\{-(\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta)\bigr\}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with the coefficient vector chosen by penalized maximum likelihood:</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\hat{\beta}\;=\;\arg\min_{\beta_{0},\beta}\;\left\{-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left[y_{i}(\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta)-\log\bigl(1+e^{\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta}\bigr)\right]+\lambda\left[\alpha\|\beta\|_{1}+(1-\alpha)\tfrac{1}{2}\|\beta\|_{2}^{2}\right]\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>β</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>{</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>log</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>λ</mi><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>β</mi><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em">+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>β</mi><msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\beta}\;=\;\arg\min_{\beta_{0},\beta}\;\left\{-\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left[y_{i}(\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta)-\log\bigl(1+e^{\beta_{0}+x_{i}^{\top}\beta}\bigr)\right]+\lambda\left[\alpha\|\beta\|_{1}+(1-\alpha)\tfrac{1}{2}\|\beta\|_{2}^{2}\right]\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The penalty in equation (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In 4.1 Elastic-net classifier and nonlinear comparators ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) is the elastic-net penalty of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zou and Hastie (2005)</a></cite>, a convex combination of the <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> lasso <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tibshirani, 1996</a>)</cite> and the <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> ridge penalty <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hoerl and Kennard, 1970</a>)</cite>. The mixing parameter
<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> interpolates between pure ridge (<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0</annotation></semantics></math>), which shrinks coefficients but retains all predictors, and pure lasso (<math id="S4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=1</annotation></semantics></math>), which produces a sparse model by zeroing some coefficients exactly. The choice of an elastic-net penalty rather than a pure lasso is dictated by the structure of the feature bank.
The <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">203</annotation></semantics></math> masked complex NDWT descriptors are heavily correlated
within and across scale and direction: log-energies at adjacent
levels within the same directional subband move together, and
persistence, energy-spectrum-slope, and adjacent-scale-difference features are algebraic combinations of the same underlying <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{j,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{j,s}</annotation></semantics></math>. In this regime the pure lasso is known to behave erratically,
arbitrarily selecting one variable from a correlated group and discarding the others; the ridge component of the elastic-net penalty stabilizes selection by encouraging strongly correlated predictors to enter or leave the model together, the so-called grouping effect of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zou and Hastie (2005)</a></cite>. We sweep <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> over a
small grid <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}</annotation></semantics></math> rather than fixing a single value, since the optimal lasso/ridge balance is task-dependent and is more usefully tuned than guessed; selection across the grid is done by inner cross-validation, as described in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The regularization strength <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> is selected for each <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> by inner <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\text{inner}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>inner</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\text{inner}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>-fold cross-validation on each outer training set, using the one-standard-error rule of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Breiman et al. (1984)</a></cite>: among the candidate values of
<math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> whose cross-validated deviance is within one standard
error of the minimum, we choose the most regularized. The 1SE rule is preferred over the minimum-deviance rule because the minimum is typically a flat, noisy region of the cross-validation curve, so choosing the smallest <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> in that flat region produces a sparser and more stable selection without sacrificing predictive performance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hastie et al., 2009</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To test whether the modality and fusion findings are specific to the linear elastic-net classifier rather than to the masked complex NDWT feature bank itself, we additionally evaluate two nonlinear classifiers under the identical patient-grouped pipeline: a support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel (<em id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">svm_radial</em>) and a gradient-boosted tree ensemble (<em id="S4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">gboost</em>). Both are fitted on the same masked complex NDWT feature vectors, partitioned by the same
patient-grouped outer folds, with the same in-fold median imputation and standardization described in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, and their hyperparameters are tuned by the same inner five-fold cross-validation used for the elastic-net path. Image-level out-of-fold probabilities from each classifier are aggregated to the patient level by the four
fusion rules of Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Patient-level prediction and fusion ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> and summarized by the
patient-cluster bootstrap of Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Patient-cluster bootstrap ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>, so that the three classifiers differ only in the function class mapping features to probabilities and not in any element of the evaluation framework.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Patient-grouped nested cross-validation</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The classifier of Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Elastic-net classifier and nonlinear comparators ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> is evaluated under repeated patient-grouped nested cross-validation. The outer loop uses <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=5</annotation></semantics></math> folds and <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=10</annotation></semantics></math> independent repeats, and the inner loop uses <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\text{inner}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>inner</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\text{inner}}=5</annotation></semantics></math> folds. Three properties of this scheme are statistically substantive and worth stating explicitly.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Patient-level partitioning.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The grouping variable introduced in Section <a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Patient identifier and grouping variable. ‣ 2 Data and patient-level structure ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is used to assign every image contributed by a single patient to the same outer fold. In each repeat we partition the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients into five approximately equal
groups, stratified on the any-positive patient label <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> of Section <a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Patient identifier and grouping variable. ‣ 2 Data and patient-level structure ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, so that no patient appears in both a training and a test partition and the class balance of the
task is preserved across folds. Image-level cross-validation, in which images from the same patient can appear in both training and test partitions, measures the classifier’s ability to predict on new images of patients it has already seen. Patient-grouped cross-validation measures the harder and more relevant quantity: prediction on new patients. The gap between the two can be
substantial <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yagis et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rouzrokh et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Varoquaux and Cheplygina, 2022</a>)</cite>; the patient-grouped partition is what
closes it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">In-fold preprocessing.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Two preprocessing steps are applied within each outer fold before the elastic-net path is fitted. Features with missing values are imputed using the per-feature median computed on the training portion of that outer fold only; all features are then centered and scaled to unit variance using the same training-fold-only statistics. Computing the imputation and
standardization statistics inside each outer fold, rather than once on the full dataset, is essential: any preprocessing that uses information from the held-out test images leaks information across
the split and biases performance estimates
upward <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kapoor and Narayanan, 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ambroise and McLachlan, 2002</a>)</cite>. This is a less visible form of leakage than the partition itself, but it has the same effect, and the patient-grouped partition does not by itself prevent it.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inner-loop model selection.</h5>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Within each outer training set, the inner <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\text{inner}}=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mtext>inner</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\text{inner}}=5</annotation></semantics></math>-fold cross-validation is used to select <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> for each candidate <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> on the elastic-net grid, again using the one-standard-error rule of
Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Elastic-net classifier and nonlinear comparators ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>. Tying model selection to an inner cross-validation, rather than to the outer test folds, prevents the selection of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> from being informed by performance on
the outer test images and is a standard requirement of nested cross-validation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Varoquaux and Cheplygina, 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The outer fold yields out-of-fold (OOF) predicted probabilities for each test image. The OOF probabilities are averaged across the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>
repeats to produce a single per-image prediction, and per-fold image-level AUCs are recorded across the <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="RK=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">RK=50</annotation></semantics></math> outer-fold fits to characterize variability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Patient-level prediction and fusion</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The classifier of Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Elastic-net classifier and nonlinear comparators ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> produces a predicted probability <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> for each individual image. Clinical decisions, however, are made at the patient level: a screening mammogram is read as a whole study, and a patient is
either recalled for further work-up or returned to routine screening on the basis of the combined evidence from all of her acquired
images <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">American College of Radiology, 2013</a>)</cite>. The classifier’s image-level probabilities therefore have to be
combined into a single per-patient probability before patient-level performance can be assessed. This combination step, sometimes called multi-view or multi-image fusion, is methodologically consequential because different aggregation rules correspond to different implicit assumptions about how the per-image evidence should be combined, and they can yield substantially different patient-level performance from the same underlying image-level
predictions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carneiro et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2020</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of out-of-fold images for patient <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, with associated probabilities <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{p_{i}:i\in\mathcal{I}(s)\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{i}:i\in\mathcal{I}(s)\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We compare four fusion rules spanning the spectrum from full averaging to extreme order-statistic selection.
The first, denoted <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>, is the arithmetic mean across all of the patient’s images,</p>
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{raw}}\;=\;\frac{1}{|\mathcal{I}(s)|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}(s)}p_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>raw</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{raw}}\;=\;\frac{1}{|\mathcal{I}(s)|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}(s)}p_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">This treats the images as exchangeable noisy estimates of a single per-patient probability, and is the implicit fusion rule when image-level out-of-fold predictions are simply pooled by averaging.
The second rule, <span id="S4.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mean views</span>, averages within each of the two standard mammographic projections (CC and MLO) and then averages the two within-view means,</p>
<table id="S4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{mv}}\;=\;\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{CC}}+\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{MLO}}\bigr)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>mv</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>MLO</mtext></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{mv}}\;=\;\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{CC}}+\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{MLO}}\bigr).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">This rule weights the two projections equally regardless of how many images of each are available. The third rule, <span id="S4.SS3.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max views</span>, replaces the outer average with a maximum,</p>
<table id="S4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{xv}}\;=\;\max\bigl\{\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{CC}},\,\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{MLO}}\bigr\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>xv</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>CC</mtext></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>MLO</mtext></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{xv}}\;=\;\max\bigl\{\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{CC}},\,\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{MLO}}\bigr\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.4" class="ltx_p">corresponding to the heuristic that a patient should be flagged on the basis of her more suspicious view. The fourth rule, <span id="S4.SS3.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span>, takes the maximum across all of the patient’s images,</p>
<table id="S4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{xi}}\;=\;\max_{i\in\mathcal{I}(s)}p_{i}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>s</mi><mtext>xi</mtext></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}_{s}^{\,\text{xi}}\;=\;\max_{i\in\mathcal{I}(s)}p_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.5" class="ltx_p">operationalizing the principle that a patient-level decision should reflect her single most suspicious image. The use of patient-level
(or exam-level) rather than image-level predictions in multi-view mammography classification was established by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carneiro et al. (2017)</a></cite>, who explicitly framed the classification target as the whole mammographic exam containing both CC and MLO views rather than the individual lesion. The
<span id="S4.SS3.p2.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> rule is the simplest aggregator consistent with that framing and admits a probabilistic interpretation as a noisy-OR combination of the per-image probabilities <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kraus et al., 2016</a>)</cite>: if each image provides an independent noisy observation of the underlying patient-level event, the maximum is the maximum-likelihood combination under the assumption that at most one positive image is needed for a positive patient.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The four rules span the natural axis from full averaging (<span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>, equal weight on every image) to extreme order-statistic selection (<span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span>, using only the maximum), with the intermediate <span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mean views</span> and <span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max views</span> testing whether view structure carries information beyond the within-view average. For the normal-versus-malignant task, the patient-level label follows the any-positive rule of Section <a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Patient identifier and grouping variable. ‣ 2 Data and patient-level structure ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>: a patient is labeled malignant if any of her retained images is malignant, and normal otherwise (the per-task form of the rule is given in Section <a href="#S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Patient identifier and grouping variable. ‣ 2 Data and patient-level structure ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). This rule matches the clinical target, detection of malignancy in at least one breast, and is the natural label partner for <span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion, which flags a
patient on her single most suspicious image; scoring an any-positive predictor against a majority-vote label would mismatch the aggregation rule and the target it is meant to estimate. Patient-level AUC is reported alongside the image-level AUC for each fusion rule. The choice of fusion rule is a methodological one rather than a heuristic,
and the four rules are compared empirically in
Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>, since the same image-level predictions can yield noticeably different patient-level AUCs depending on how they
are combined.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Patient-cluster bootstrap</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The cross-validation scheme of Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> provides point estimates of patient-level AUC, but not the uncertainty around those estimates. Patient-grouped cross-validation controls bias in the point estimate by enforcing leakage-free partitions;
the patient-cluster bootstrap described in this subsection is its inferential complement, attributing the variance around the point
estimate to the right unit of statistical replication. The combination of the two — CV for bias control, cluster bootstrap for variance attribution — is what makes the AUC differences
reported in Sections <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>—<a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> interpretable as statements about the patient population rather than about a particular fold structure or image collection.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The standard nonparametric bootstrap of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Efron (1979)</a></cite> resamples observations independently and is not directly applicable here. The unit of statistical replication in our analysis is the patient rather than the image, and the images contributed by a single patient are correlated:
they share anatomy, acquisition geometry, and pathology. We therefore use the patient-cluster bootstrap, in which the resampling unit is the patient rather than the image <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Field and Welsh, 2007</a>)</cite>. For each reported AUC we draw <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=2{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=2{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> bootstrap resamples with replacement at the patient level, with each resample retaining every image contributed by the drawn patients so that the within-patient correlation structure of the original sample is preserved exactly. The patient-level AUC is recomputed on each resampled set, and the <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5</annotation></semantics></math>th and <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>97.5</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.5</annotation></semantics></math>th empirical percentiles of the resulting bootstrap distribution give the <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence interval reported in the results. When AUCs from competing models are compared, for example CM-only versus
DM-only or one fusion rule versus another, the same <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> patient-level resamples are reused for both models, so that the two models are evaluated on the same simulated patient population at every iteration and the AUC difference is taken within each resample. This is the bootstrap analogue of a paired comparison: any variability driven by which patients happen to appear in a given resample cancels out of the difference rather than inflating it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The patient-cluster bootstrap has two practical advantages over alternative inference procedures for AUC. First, unlike the DeLong test <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">DeLong et al., 1988</a>)</cite>, it does not rely on the asymptotic normality of the AUC statistic, and, more importantly, it does not assume
independent observations — an assumption that a clustered design violates, since each patient contributes several correlated images. Applied to image-level AUCs, the DeLong procedure would understate uncertainty for the same within-patient correlation reason that motivates the patient-grouped cross-validation of Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>. Second, unlike a standard non-clustered bootstrap, which resamples images independently and so breaks the within-patient correlation structure, the patient-cluster bootstrap resamples whole patients and retains every image of each drawn patient, so the uncertainty it reports is attached to the patient — the level at which the model must generalize — rather than to the image.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Results</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Patient-grouped baseline</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We begin by evaluating four binary diagnostic tasks — normal versus malignant, normal versus abnormal (benign or malignant), benign versus malignant, and normal versus benign — under the patient-grouped
framework of Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Patient-grouped nested cross-validation ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, applied to the pooled DM+CM training set, both image types as rows with a binary contrast-type indicator. For each task, we report the image-level AUC computed from pooled out-of-fold probabilities, the patient-level AUC obtained from <span id="S5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> fusion across each patient’s images, and 95% confidence intervals constructed by the patient-cluster bootstrap procedure described in Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Patient-cluster bootstrap ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>. The complete set of point estimates and confidence intervals is collected in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and displayed graphically in Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T2" class="ltx_table">

<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/forest_four_tasks.png" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/217;" width="452" height="217" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The clearest pattern in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> and
Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is the ordering of the four tasks by separability. Normal-versus-malignant discrimination is substantially the strongest, with patient-level AUC <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.834" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.834</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.834</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.781" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.781</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.781</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math>) and an image-level AUC of <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>
(<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.772" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.772</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.772</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.838" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.838</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.838</annotation></semantics></math>). Benign-versus-malignant is the next-strongest contrast, with patient-level AUC <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.708" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.708</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.708</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.646" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.646</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.646</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.774" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.774</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.774</annotation></semantics></math>), separated from normal-versus-malignant but with overlapping intervals. The normal-versus-abnormal task (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.648" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.648</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.648</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.567" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.567</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.567</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.723" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.723</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.723</annotation></semantics></math>) and the
normal-versus-benign task (<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.598" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.598</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.598</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.529" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.529</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.529</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.662" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.662</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.662</annotation></semantics></math>) are weaker, with wide patient-level intervals whose lower bounds approach <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.52" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.52</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.52</annotation></semantics></math>. This
ordering is consistent with the radiological intuition that contrast uptake on CESM is most informative for distinguishing healthy tissue
from frank malignancy, while benign lesions can resemble either malignancies or normal tissue depending on their composition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The point estimates in Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> are stable to the choice of cross-validation partition: image-level AUC standard deviations across the ten outer-CV repeats lie between <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.003" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.003</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.003</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.006" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.006</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.006</annotation></semantics></math> for every task, and the bootstrap intervals, computed under a separate form of resampling, are correspondingly narrow.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In several tasks the patient-level AUC exceeds the image-level AUC (for normal-versus-malignant, <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.834" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.834</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.834</annotation></semantics></math> versus <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>), which may seem
counterintuitive but follows directly from how the two quantities are defined. Every image inherits its breast-level label, so a malignant patient contributes both the few images on which the malignancy is visible and the several uninformative images — the contralateral breast and unaffected views — that look essentially normal and are
scored low by the classifier. At the image level these uninformative images are labeled malignant yet ranked low, and they count against the image-level AUC. Aggregating a patient’s images into a single
score by <span id="S5.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> averages out this within-patient noise: the informative images pull the patient’s mean up enough to rank her correctly, and the uninformative images are absorbed into one
per-patient value rather than counted as individual ranking errors. The patient-level estimate is therefore the average of several noisy per-image predictions, which is a lower-variance estimate of the quantity of interest than any single image provides. This image-to-patient improvement is distinct from, and in the opposite direction to, the image-level <em id="S5.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">inflation</em> produced by information leakage (Section <a href="#S1" title="1 Introduction ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>): the inflation arises when a patient’s images straddle the train/test split so the model recognizes the patient rather than the disease, whereas the improvement described here arises under a strictly patient-grouped partition, where no such leakage is possible and the only effect of aggregation is to reduce per-patient variance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The gap between the patient-grouped and image-level cross-validation estimates on the same data is the more substantive check. For the normal-versus-malignant task, image-level five-fold cross-validation (Supplement S4) yields an image-level AUC of <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.818" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.818</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.818</annotation></semantics></math>, only <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.012" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.012</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.012</annotation></semantics></math> above the patient-grouped image-level estimate of
<math id="S5.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>. A feature bank that had memorized patient-specific structure rather than learning generalizable signal would lose far more performance when patient identity is removed from the partitioning.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Rather than inheriting the large worst-case inflation reported in settings such as slice-level brain MRI (Section <a href="#S1" title="1 Introduction ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), the feature bank shows almost no image-to-patient gap here, consistent with patients contributing roughly eight moderately correlated images rather than dozens of near-identical slices. Its near-absence is reassurance that the modality, fusion-rule, and classifier comparisons that follow reflect properties of the feature representation, not leakage between training and test partitions.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.1.1 </span>Discrimination floor on benign-versus-malignant</h4>

<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Benign-versus-malignant is the clinically meaningful next step beyond “is there cancer or not,” but its patient-level AUC of <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.708" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.708</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.708</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.646" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.646</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.646</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.774" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.774</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.774</annotation></semantics></math>) is markedly weaker than normal-versus-malignant. The question is whether this shortfall is a limitation of the wavelet feature bank or of the contrast itself at this sample size. Two findings indicate the latter.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, a pretrained ResNet-50 frozen-feature representation, run on the same patients under identical patient-grouped folds, does no better.
Under <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion the wavelet bank reaches <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.713" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.713</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.713</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.650" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.650</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.650</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.778" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.778</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.778</annotation></semantics></math>) on CM and <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.690" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.690</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.690</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.625" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.625</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.625</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.753" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.753</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.753</annotation></semantics></math>) on DM+CM, and ResNet-50 reaches <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.746" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.746</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.746</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.687" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.687</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.687</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>) and <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.710" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.710</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.710</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.645" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.645</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.645</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.770" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.770</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.770</annotation></semantics></math>) on the same patients; all four intervals overlap substantially and the two representations are within about <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math> AUC everywhere (full results in Supplement S3). A much stronger representation does not rescue the task.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Second, the <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion lift that helps
normal-versus-malignant (Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>) disappears here: across the four representation–modality cells the four fusion rules
fall within <math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.02" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.02</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.02</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math> of one another, and for the wavelet DM+CM cell <span id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> is in fact the lowest. This is what one expects when benign and malignant lesions overlap in their CESM
enhancement far more than either does with normal tissue; no single image is decisively more suspicious, so flagging on the most suspicious image buys nothing.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.SSS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The benign-versus-malignant contrast on CDD-CESM is therefore task-limited, not representation-limited. The remaining analyses focus on normal-versus-malignant, the most clinically actionable task and the one on which the dataset supports the most informative inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A central methodological question raised in Section <a href="#S1" title="1 Introduction ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> is how much of the malignancy-relevant signal lives in each of the two
acquired CESM image types when the same masked complex NDWT feature bank is applied to each. To answer it, we re-ran the normal-versus-malignant pipeline separately on the low-energy images (DM only), the recombined contrast images (CM only), and the pooled set of both image types (DM+CM). In the DM+CM configuration the DM and CM images enter as separate training rows rather than being concatenated
into a joint feature vector, so the predictor count is the 203 wavelet descriptors used by each single-modality model plus one binary contrast-type indicator distinguishing the two acquisitions, 204 predictors in total. The patient-grouped folds and bootstrap resamples were held fixed across the three configurations so that the differences in AUC are attributable to the choice of modality alone. Image- and patient-level ROC curves for each configuration are shown in Figure <a href="#S5.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, and the corresponding AUCs with 95% patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals are displayed in
Figure <a href="#S5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/three_ROC.png" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/156;" width="476" height="156" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F3.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S5.F3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">ROC curves for the normal-versus-malignant task under the three modality configurations. Image-level curves (blue) are computed from pooled out-of-fold probabilities; patient-level curves (red) use
<span id="S5.F3.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> fusion. The three configurations are closely comparable, with image-level AUCs of <math id="S5.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.823" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.823</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.823</annotation></semantics></math> (DM), <math id="S5.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math> (CM), and <math id="S5.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math> (DM+CM), and patient-level <span id="S5.F3.6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> AUCs clustered near <math id="S5.F3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.81" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.81</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.81</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.F3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.83" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.83</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.83</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/AUC_patient_cluster_bootstrap.png" id="S5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/177;" width="476" height="177" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Patient-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for image- and patient-level AUC on the normal-versus-malignant task, separately for the three modality configurations. The three configurations overlap substantially at both evaluation scales; no modality separates from the others beyond bootstrap noise, although DM+CM is highest at the patient level by point estimate.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two findings stand out. First, the three modality configurations are statistically indistinguishable on the normal-versus-malignant task. At the image level the AUCs are <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.823" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.823</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.823</annotation></semantics></math> (DM), <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math> (CM), and <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math> (DM+CM); at the patient level under <span id="S5.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> fusion they are
<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.814" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.814</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.814</annotation></semantics></math> (DM, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.756" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.756</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.756</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.866" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.866</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.866</annotation></semantics></math>), <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.811" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.811</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.811</annotation></semantics></math> (CM, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.755" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.755</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.755</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.865" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.865</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.865</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.834" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.834</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.834</annotation></semantics></math> (DM+CM, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.781" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.781</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.781</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math>), with every pairwise bootstrap interval overlapping substantially. The recombined
contrast image and the low-energy image therefore carry comparable malignancy-relevant signal when the same masked complex NDWT feature bank is applied to each. This runs counter to the expectation that the
contrast image, engineered to suppress background tissue and highlight iodine uptake, should dominate: the low-energy image is an equally informative substrate for this feature bank. The two acquisitions
nonetheless recover that comparable signal through largely disjoint, physically interpretable feature families (Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>), so the equivalence in accuracy does not imply redundancy in mechanism.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Second, pooling DM and CM is the strongest configuration at the patient level, though by a margin within bootstrap noise rather than a decisive one. The DM+CM patient-level AUC of <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.834" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.834</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.834</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>) and <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math> (<span id="S5.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span>, Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>) edges both single-modality models at every fusion rule, while its image-level AUC (<math id="S5.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>) is marginally below the two single-modality models. Because the pooled model fits a single shared coefficient vector across both image types and draws on the disjoint feature families each modality
supplies, the combined configuration loses nothing relative to either alone and is modestly stronger once predictions are aggregated to the patient level. From a deployment standpoint, a single-modality CM-only or DM-only pipeline remains a defensible simplification, since neither is distinguishable from the combined model at the patient level on this dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The image-level versus patient-level gap also differs across configurations. The single-modality models and the combined model move differently from image-level to patient-level evaluation: combining the two modalities doubles the number of images per patient that enter the <span id="S5.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> fusion, and averaging across a larger image set reduces per-patient variance in the fused probability. The gap, in other words, is sensitive to the number of images being averaged, not only to the underlying classifier. We return to this point in Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a>, where the fusion-rule comparison shows that the gap is also strongly modulated by which images are aggregated.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Stable feature selection across modalities</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The modality comparison of Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> establishes that the DM-only and CM-only configurations reach statistically indistinguishable patient-level AUC on the normal-versus-malignant task. This raises a mechanistic question: do the two image types reach comparable accuracy by drawing on the same descriptors, or by different routes through the feature bank? To address it, we recorded the
elastic-net selection frequency of every feature across all outer-fold fits of the normal-versus-malignant pipeline, separately for the three
modality configurations. A feature is considered <em id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">stably selected</em> if it appears in the active set of at least <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the fitted models; the top thirty stably selected features across the three
configurations are displayed in Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/Figure_19.png" id="S5.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/275;" width="476" height="275" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S5.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Selection frequency of the top thirty stably selected features across outer-fold fits of the normal-versus-malignant pipeline, shown separately for the CM-only, DM-only, and DM+CM
configurations. Color encodes the fraction of outer-fold fits in which each feature has a non-zero elastic-net coefficient. The right margin labels each feature by its descriptor family. Phase-coherence and phase-resultant descriptors are selected in nearly every DM-only fit and almost never in the CM-only model, while the CM-only model
concentrates on a set of magnitude and log-energy descriptors.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
