<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The pattern in Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> is the central mechanistic finding of the paper. The DM-only and CM-only models, applied to images of the same patients with the same masked complex
NDWT feature bank, reach equivalent accuracy through largely disjoint feature sets. The phase-coherence and phase-resultant descriptors are the clearest case. The most prominent examples are the level-1 and level-2 phase-resultant and
inter-channel phase-coherence descriptors, which are selected in nearly every DM-only
outer-fold fit and essentially never in the CM-only fits. The persistence and anisotropy descriptors show the same asymmetry: features such as <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">L1_frac_D</span>,
<span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">V_max_over_levels_Q95</span>, and
<span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">H_adjacent_scale_corr_mean</span> are selected by nearly every DM-only fit and rarely by the CM-only model, as are several adjacent-scale log-energy differences such as <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">V_L5_minus_L4_log2energy</span> and <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">D_L2_minus_L1_log2energy</span> (though the direction is not uniform across this family — <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">D_L6_minus_L5_log2energy</span>, for instance, is selected predominantly by the CM-only model). The
CM-only model in turn concentrates on a largely separate set: magnitude coefficient-of-variation and persistence descriptors such as <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">D_L3_mag_CV</span> and <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">H_max_over_levels_mean</span> (both at <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math> selection) and the energy-spectrum <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> feature
<span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">V_R2_L2_L7</span> (<math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>96</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96\%</annotation></semantics></math>), each of which is rarely or never selected by the DM-only model. A smaller number of magnitude descriptors are selected by both models — chiefly broadband coefficient-of-variation features such as <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">H_L7_mag_CV</span>
(selected in essentially every CM-only fit and in roughly three-quarters of DM-only fits) and <span id="S5.SS3.p2.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">H_L6_mag_CV</span> — so the disjointness is
specific to the phase channel and the geometric descriptors rather than total. The DM+CM column shows a hybrid pattern: features from both
groups appear, reflecting that the combined model has access to both signal carriers and the elastic-net penalty distributes weight between them.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The disjointness of the selected feature sets has a physical interpretation that explains how the DM-only and CM-only models reach comparable patient-level AUC while sharing few descriptors. The DM
image is a conventional mammogram that depicts overall tissue density and architectural organization; the signal that distinguishes
malignant from normal tissue in this image is geometric, such as distortion of fibroglandular patterns, oriented texture irregularities, and disrupted local coherence. It is best captured by features that summarize the phase of complex wavelet coefficients, since phase coherence indexes how consistently local oriented structure is organized within a scale. The CM image, in contrast, suppresses background tissue and selectively highlights iodine uptake; the malignancy signal here is intensity-localized rather than geometric, and is best captured by features that summarize the magnitude distribution of the wavelet coefficients; in particular the coefficient of variation, which is large when energy is concentrated in a small fraction of the tissue support. The masked complex NDWT framework adapts to whichever signal carrier is dominant in a given modality, drawing on its phase summaries when the image is geometric and on its magnitude summaries when the image is intensity-localized. This adaptive behavior is not a property of the elastic-net classifier in isolation; it is a property of the feature bank, which provides both
phase and magnitude descriptors at every scale and direction and lets the classifier select among them. The two acquisitions thus encode comparable malignancy information through different physical channels, and the feature bank is expressive enough to read both, which is why the modality equivalence of Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> coexists with near-disjoint feature selection rather than implying redundancy between the two image types.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Patient-level fusion</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next ask how the choice of fusion rule (Section <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Patient-level prediction and fusion ‣ 4 Modeling and inference framework ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>) affects the patient-level AUC, holding the underlying image-level
predictions fixed. The four rules — <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>, <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mean views</span>, <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max views</span>, and <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> — were applied to the same out-of-fold image probabilities used in Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>, separately for each of the three modality configurations. The resulting patient-level AUCs and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals are displayed in Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/fusion_bars.png" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/217;" width="452" height="217" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Patient-level AUC under four fusion rules, for each of the three modality configurations. The <span id="S5.F6.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>, <span id="S5.F6.8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mean views</span>, and <span id="S5.F6.8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max views</span> rules give nearly identical patient-level AUCs within each configuration; the <span id="S5.F6.8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> rule lifts the patient-level AUC by roughly <math id="S5.F6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.F6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.07</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.07</annotation></semantics></math> in every configuration. Error bars are <math id="S5.F6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo mathsize="1.110em">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> patient-cluster bootstrap percentile intervals.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The pattern in Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> divides the four rules into two groups. The three averaging-style rules — <span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span>, <span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mean views</span>, and <span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max views</span> — behave similarly within each modality, indicating that how the
within-view averaging is organized (whether views are weighted equally or compared at the view level) matters relatively little. What does matter is whether the patient-level summary is an average
at all. The <span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> rule, which abandons averaging entirely and reports the patient on her single most suspicious image, separates from the other three in every modality configuration, with the largest gain over <span id="S5.SS4.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> on the
single-modality models. The size of the lift (roughly
0.04–0.07 patient-level AUC across modalities) is reproduced when the feature bank is changed to ResNet-50 (Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>), so it is a property of the fusion rule rather than of the particular feature representation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Averaging dilutes the signal for a simple clinical reason. Of a patient’s eight or so images, only the two or three views of the affected breast carry visible malignancy; the contralateral breast and unaffected views look essentially normal and are scored low. Averaging pulls the high probability of the informative images toward these low ones, so the patient-level estimate mixes evidence with non-evidence. The maximum instead returns the single most confident image, letting the patient-level summary reflect the strongest finding rather than the average across the study.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This is the same logic that radiologists apply when assigning a final BI-RADS category from a multi-view mammographic exam: the overall assessment reflects the most suspicious finding, not the
average across views <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">American College of Radiology, 2013</a>; <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zonderland and Smithuis, 2014</a>)</cite>. Applied as an aggregation rule on classifier probabilities, the same
heuristic gives better patient-level discrimination than averaging. Under <span id="S5.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion, the CM-only model achieves a patient-level AUC of <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.827</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.827</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.918" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.918</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.918</annotation></semantics></math>) and the DM+CM model achieves <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.840" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.840</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.840</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.923" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.923</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.923</annotation></semantics></math>); the DM-only model reaches <math id="S5.SS4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.855" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.855</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.855</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS4.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.901" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.901</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.901</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Three observations follow. The first is that the framework reaches patient-level AUC near <math id="S5.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.88" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.88</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.88</annotation></semantics></math> on the most clinically actionable contrast in this dataset, using a model in which every retained predictor is a named, physically interpretable wavelet descriptor. The classifier is small, fast to train, and transparent at the level of named
wavelet-feature groups and selected predictors.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The second is that the three modality configurations remain close under <span id="S5.SS4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion, as under the averaging rules (Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>): DM, CM, and DM+CM reach <math id="S5.SS4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.855" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.855</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.855</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math> respectively, with overlapping bootstrap intervals. The combined configuration is highest by point estimate, but a single-modality pipeline incurs no statistically discernible
loss, so a classification pipeline can be built from either acquisition alone with no measurable cost in patient-level performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The third is that how the per-image predictions are combined into a patient-level prediction matters more than is usually acknowledged. The gap between averaging across images and taking the most suspicious image is on the order of <math id="S5.SS4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS4.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.07</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.07</annotation></semantics></math> AUC, large enough that two papers using the same underlying classifier can report substantially different patient-level performance just by choosing
different fusion rules. Fusion choice should therefore be reported explicitly in any CESM classifier evaluation, alongside the classifier itself.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Robustness to classifier choice</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The modality-equivalence finding is not an artifact of the linear elastic-net classifier. We re-ran the normal-versus-malignant pipeline with a radial-basis SVM and a gradient-boosted tree ensemble, holding the feature bank, patient-grouped folds, fusion rules, and bootstrap resamples fixed, and compared the three classifiers at the patient level under <span id="S5.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion. The patient-level AUCs are displayed in Figure <a href="#S5.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 5.5 Robustness to classifier choice ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Two patterns hold across all three classifiers. First, the elastic-net model is not statistically outperformed by either nonlinear classifier. On every modality the three classifiers fall within a narrow band whose bootstrap intervals overlap substantially, so no
classifier separates from the others by a margin the dataset can resolve: on DM the three patient-level AUCs are <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.807" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.807</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.807</annotation></semantics></math> (elastic-net), <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math> (SVM), and <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.815" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.815</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.815</annotation></semantics></math> (gradient boosting); on CM they are <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.856" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.856</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.856</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S5.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.818" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.818</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.818</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.843" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.843</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.843</annotation></semantics></math>; on DM+CM they are <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.837" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.837</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.837</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.830" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.830</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.830</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.817" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.817</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.817</annotation></semantics></math>. The SVM and gradient-boosting estimates reach patient-level AUC of approximately <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.84" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.84</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.84</annotation></semantics></math> at their best modality, neither exceeding the
elastic-net estimate beyond bootstrap noise. These figures are not directly comparable to the headline elastic-net AUCs of Sections <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a> and <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>: to give the three classifiers a common tuning budget, the classifier comparison fixes the elastic-net mixing parameter at <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.5</annotation></semantics></math> with a coarser regularization path, whereas the headline pipeline sweeps <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> over
<math id="S5.SS5.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{0.3,0.5,0.7\}</annotation></semantics></math> on a finer path, so the elastic-net column here is internally consistent with the SVM and gradient-boosting columns rather than with the full-pipeline AUCs reported elsewhere. Second, the modality equivalence reported in Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> is reproduced under each classifier rather than overturned by it: no configuration is reliably
strongest across the three classifiers. The best modality is in fact different for each classifier — DM+CM for the SVM, CM for gradient boosting, and CM for the elastic-net — and in every case the
bootstrap intervals of the three modalities overlap, so the apparent ordering shifts with the classifier precisely because the three modalities are statistically indistinguishable. The absence of a
stable modality ranking across classifiers is exactly what the modality-equivalence finding predicts, and it confirms that the equivalence is a property of the masked complex NDWT feature bank and the patient-grouped evaluation rather than of the linear model.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The practical reading is that the elastic-net classifier, chosen for its sparsity, speed, and per-feature interpretability, sacrifices no measurable patient-level discrimination to two more flexible function classes on this feature representation. The conclusions of Sections <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> and <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a> are properties of the masked complex NDWT feature bank and the patient-grouped evaluation, not of the particular classifier used to read it.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/Figure_20.png" id="S5.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/407;" width="476" height="407" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="S5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Patient-level ROC curves for the normal-versus-malignant task under max image
fusion, stratified by classifier and modality. The panels show that modality ordering is not
stable across classifier families, consistent with the bootstrap interval results.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To benchmark the masked complex NDWT feature bank against a deep-learning representation, we substituted the <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}048</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional
activations of the global average pooling layer of an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al., 2016</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Deng et al., 2009</a>)</cite>
for the <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">203</annotation></semantics></math> wavelet features and ran the resulting design through the same patient-grouped pipeline (same folds, classifier, fusion
rules, and bootstrap). This frozen-feature protocol is the standard transfer-learning baseline when end-to-end fine-tuning is not
feasible <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sharif Razavian et al., 2014</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yosinski et al., 2014</a>)</cite>, and pits a purpose-built domain representation of <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">203</annotation></semantics></math> predictors against a generic representation of ten times the dimensionality, pretrained on millions of natural
images.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under <span id="S5.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion, the wavelet and ResNet-50 representations reach patient-level AUCs whose bootstrap intervals overlap in all three modality configurations: wavelet <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.855" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.855</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.855</annotation></semantics></math>
(<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.901" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.901</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.901</annotation></semantics></math>) versus ResNet <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.814" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.814</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.814</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.758" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.758</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.758</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.869" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.869</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.869</annotation></semantics></math>) on DM, <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.918" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.918</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.918</annotation></semantics></math>) versus <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.888" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.888</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.888</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.846" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.846</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.846</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.927" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.927</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.927</annotation></semantics></math>) on CM, and
<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.840" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.840</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.840</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.923" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.923</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.923</annotation></semantics></math>) versus <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.881" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.881</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.881</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.838" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.838</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.838</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.924" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.924</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.924</annotation></semantics></math>) on DM+CM (Figure <a href="#S5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ 5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>). The point estimates differ most on DM, where the wavelet bank is higher by <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.041" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.041</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.041</annotation></semantics></math>, and least on
DM+CM, where the two are within <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.002</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.002</annotation></semantics></math>; on CM, ResNet is higher by <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.014" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.014</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.014</annotation></semantics></math>. In none of the three configurations does the difference exceed
bootstrap noise, so the two representations are statistically indistinguishable at the patient level despite the deep representation having ten times the dimensionality.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/wavelet_vs_neural_net_2.png" id="S5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/147;" width="381" height="147" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S5.F8.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Patient-level AUC under <span id="S5.F8.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion for the masked complex NDWT feature bank (blue circles) and the ResNet-50 frozen-feature baseline (orange squares), on the three modality configurations. Bootstrap 95% CIs overlap substantially across all three configurations.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="S5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2607.02394v1/wavelet_vs_neural_net.png" id="S5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/190;" width="333" height="190" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F9.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Wavelet vs ResNet-50 frozen features under matched patient-grouped cross-validation. Left: image-level AUC. Right: patient-level AUC under <span id="S5.F9.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion. The image-level
edge of the ResNet representation narrows at the patient level. Error bars are 95% patient-cluster bootstrap intervals (<math id="S5.F9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=2000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=2000</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At the image level the ResNet-50 representation is somewhat stronger than the wavelet bank (ResNet <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.833" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.833</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.833</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.858" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.858</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.858</annotation></semantics></math> versus wavelet
<math id="S5.SS6.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.823" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.823</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.823</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.827</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.827</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math> on DM, CM, and DM+CM respectively). On CM and DM+CM this edge narrows under <span id="S5.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion at the patient
level, where the two representations become statistically indistinguishable; on DM the patient-level ordering in fact reverses,
the wavelet bank moving from <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.010" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.010</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.010</annotation></semantics></math> behind at the image level to <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.041" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.041</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.041</annotation></semantics></math> ahead at the patient level, though with overlapping intervals at both scales. The ancillary fusion finding of the wavelet pipeline is also reproduced under the ResNet features: the <span id="S5.SS6.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> lift
over averaging-style fusion holds for the ResNet bank too, showing that the fusion-rule result of Section <a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Patient-level fusion ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a> is not specific to the wavelet feature bank.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The parity itself is the substantive result, but its consequences for a radiologist using the model are what make it matter. The wavelet predictors map onto categories that are already used to read mammograms: oriented phase coherence indexes architectural distortion and spiculation, the dominant DM-image cues for malignancy in the
BI-RADS lexicon <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">American College of Radiology, 2013</a>)</cite>; magnitude distribution on CM indexes localized iodine uptake, the dominant CM cue. A flagged case
can therefore be inspected at the level of specific scale-direction descriptors and traced back to image regions a radiologist could verify
against the imaging finding. This per-feature physical correspondence is the property that distinguishes the wavelet representation from a
generic deep representation of comparable patient-level accuracy, and the property that makes the parity result reported here a substantive
methodological contribution rather than a horse-race outcome.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The same qualitative parity pattern — the wavelet and ResNet-50 representations producing overlapping patient-cluster bootstrap intervals at the patient level — holds on the harder
benign-versus-malignant contrast (Section <a href="#S5.SS1.SSS1" title="5.1.1 Discrimination floor on benign-versus-malignant ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1.1</span></a>, Supplement S3), where both representations achieve substantially lower absolute performance but remain close to one another in every modality configuration. The parity finding is therefore not specific to the strongest contrast: under leakage-free evaluation on this dataset, the interpretable wavelet representation and the deep ResNet-50 representation reach comparable patient-level
accuracy whether the task is well-separated (normal versus malignant) or near the limit of what the dataset supports (benign versus malignant).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In short, the 203-dimensional interpretable wavelet bank shows no statistically discernible
patient-level AUC loss relative to a generic deep representation ten times its size, while retaining a feature selection profile that matches the categories radiologists already use to read CESM mammograms.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Discussion</h2>

<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The two image types carry equivalent signal through different channels</h5>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The central modality finding is one of equivalence. On the normal-versus-malignant task the DM-only, CM-only, and DM+CM configurations reach statistically indistinguishable patient-level AUC, with overlapping patient-cluster bootstrap intervals under every
fusion rule and under all three classifier families
(Sections <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Modality comparison: DM, CM, and DM + CM ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> and <a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5 Robustness to classifier choice ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a>). The recombined contrast image does not dominate the low-energy image, as the acquisition design might lead one to expect; the two acquisitions
are comparably informative inputs to the masked complex NDWT feature bank. This is a stronger and more surprising statement than a simple ranking of the two image types would be. The CM image is engineered to suppress background tissue and isolate iodine uptake, and the natural expectation is that a malignancy classifier should read it more accurately than the conventional low-energy image; instead, the
low-energy image carries an equal amount of malignancy-relevant signal once the feature bank is allowed to summarize both the magnitude and the phase of its wavelet coefficients. Pooling the two image types is highest at the patient level by point estimate but not by a margin the dataset can resolve, so a single-modality pipeline, built from either
acquisition alone, is a defensible simplification that loses no measurable patient-level performance. The same equivalence holds for the ResNet-50 frozen-feature representation (Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>), so it is a property of the dataset and the patient-grouped evaluation rather than an artifact of the wavelet representation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A practical consequence is that the common deep-learning default of using both acquisitions together is not required for this task at this dataset size: either image type alone supports comparable patient-level discrimination, and the choice between them can be made on grounds of acquisition cost or dose rather than expected accuracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Equivalent accuracy is reached through disjoint, physically interpretable feature channels</h5>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The equivalence in accuracy does not imply redundancy in mechanism. The DM-only and CM-only models reach their comparable patient-level AUC through largely disjoint feature sets (Section <a href="#S5.SS3" title="5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.3</span></a>, Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5.3 Stable feature selection across modalities ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). The
DM-only model is essentially a phase model: the top phase-resultant and phase-coherence features are selected in <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>90</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math> of DM-only outer folds and in essentially none of the CM-only folds. The CM-only model in turn concentrates on magnitude-distribution and energy-spectrum descriptors, chiefly coefficient-of-variation features, that the DM-only model rarely selects. The two acquisitions therefore encode
comparable malignancy information through different physical channels: geometric, oriented structure on the low-energy image, read by the phase channel of the complex transform, and intensity-localized iodine
uptake on the contrast image, read by the magnitude channel.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To our knowledge, this is among the first demonstrations that complex-wavelet phase
summaries carry substantial mammographic malignancy signal under leakage-free,
patient-grouped evaluation, and it appears to be the first such demonstration in the
CDD-CESM setting.
The pattern is consistent with the radiological intuition that malignancy detection on the low-energy image relies heavily on architectural disruption,
including spiculation, distortion, and asymmetric oriented patterns, which is encoded in the relative phase of oriented wavelet coefficients rather than in their magnitudes. A real-valued wavelet transform would
not give the classifier access to the phase channel at all, and a magnitude-only feature bank derived from a complex transform would discard it after the fact. The complex non-decimated wavelet transform preserves both magnitude and phase across scales, and the classifier
draws on whichever is more informative for the image type at hand; it is precisely this dual availability that allows two physically different acquisitions to be read with equal accuracy by a single feature bank. The role of complex wavelets in capturing oriented
texture has a long methodological history in statistical signal processing <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vidaković, 1999</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kingsbury, 2001</a>)</cite>; the contribution of the present analysis is to show that the phase channel
of such a transform, when summarized over an anatomical mask and evaluated under patient-grouped cross-validation, carries detectable malignancy signal at a sample size of <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients, and that it does
so on the very image type the contrast acquisition was designed to improve upon.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fusion rule choice is consequential and underreported</h5>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The gap between <span id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">raw mean</span> and <span id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion is around <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.04" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.04</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.04</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.07</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.07</annotation></semantics></math> AUC and is reproduced under a different feature representation (ResNet-50, Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>), so it is not
specific to the wavelet bank. This makes a methodological point that extends beyond the present feature bank: when image-level classifiers are deployed on patients with multiple acquisitions, the choice of fusion rule is consequential, and the rule most closely aligned with the radiological principle that the final assessment is
driven by the most suspicious finding, max image fusion, also gives the highest empirical
AUC in this task. Reports that pool multi image patient predictions by averaging, as much of the deep-learning CESM literature implicitly does, may understate achievable patient-level performance. We recommend that fusion rule be reported explicitly in any multi-image medical classification study, alongside the classifier, the cross-validation scheme, and the unit of statistical replication; absent that information, two papers using the same underlying
classifier can report substantially different patient-level performance figures without the difference being attributable to anything beyond aggregation choice. The lift is also notably contrast-dependent: on the
harder benign-versus-malignant task, where benign and malignant lesions overlap in their enhancement patterns far more than either does with normal tissue, the <span id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> advantage disappears (Section <a href="#S5.SS1.SSS1" title="5.1.1 Discrimination floor on benign-versus-malignant ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1.1</span></a>), so the benefit of single-image fusion is specific to tasks in which the malignancy signal is concentrated in a small number of a patient’s images rather than spread across them.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interpretable representations match deep representations
under correct evaluation</h5>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Under matched patient-grouped evaluation the ResNet-50 frozen-feature representation produces higher image-level AUC than the wavelet feature bank, with a clear margin on DM+CM, but this edge disappears at the
patient level under <span id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> fusion: across all three modality configurations the bootstrap intervals for the two representations overlap substantially. The pattern is informative in two ways. First, it indicates that part of the image-level advantage of the deeper representation reflects a finer-grained per-image signal that does not translate into a patient-level advantage once images are
aggregated by the maximum; within-patient variation in image quality, view, and contralateral imaging carries less weight under <span id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">max image</span> than under averaging-style fusion. Second, it sharpens the interpretable-versus-opaque tradeoff for this task: at the clinically relevant level of aggregation, the <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="203" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>203</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">203</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional wavelet bank gives up no measurable AUC to a <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,048</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}048</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional ImageNet-pretrained representation, and recovers in exchange a feature-selection profile in which every retained predictor has a named physical meaning. The same qualitative parity holds on the harder benign-versus-malignant contrast (Section <a href="#S5.SS1.SSS1" title="5.1.1 Discrimination floor on benign-versus-malignant ‣ 5.1 Patient-grouped baseline ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1.1</span></a>), at substantially lower absolute performance for both representations, so the parity finding generalizes across the range of task difficulty this dataset supports.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Limitations</h5>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The CDD-CESM dataset is single-source and modest in scale; the feature-selection patterns and modality comparisons reported here should be reassessed on an independent CESM cohort when one becomes available. Each image’s breast label is treated as the ground truth for the image, which is correct for contralateral comparisons but cannot capture lesion location or extent at the image level. The patient-cluster bootstrap uses percentile intervals. Bias-corrected and accelerated
cluster-bootstrap intervals could also be considered, especially if future studies use smaller
or more imbalanced cohorts; we did not rely on them here because the reported conclusions
are based mainly on paired bootstrap overlap and qualitative stability across configurations. The elastic-net classifier is linear in the
wavelet features; nonlinear interactions between features may exist that the linear model cannot capture, though the classifier-comparison
results in Section <a href="#S5.SS5" title="5.5 Robustness to classifier choice ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.5</span></a> suggest that any such interactions are not substantial for this representation. Finally, the deep-learning comparison in Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Comparison with a deep-learning feature representation ‣ 5 Results ‣ Masked complex non-decimated wavelet features for patient-level classification of contrast-enhanced mammography" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a> uses a
frozen-feature transfer-learning baseline rather than an end-to-end fine-tuned network; this was a deliberate design choice given the dataset size, since fine-tuning a network of ResNet-50’s capacity on
<math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="308" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>308</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">308</annotation></semantics></math> patients under patient-grouped cross-validation carries substantial overfitting risk. A fine-tuned configuration evaluated under the same patient-grouped folds is the natural extension of the present comparison and is left to future work.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We have built and evaluated a patient-level interpretable classification framework for contrast-enhanced spectral mammography, combining a masked complex non-decimated wavelet feature bank with an
elastic-net logistic classifier. Under repeated patient-grouped nested cross-validation with patient-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals on
the CDD-CESM dataset, the framework achieves patient-level AUC of <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.874</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.874</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%~\text{CI}~0.827" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>CI</mtext><mo lspace="0.330em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>0.827</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%~\text{CI}~0.827</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.918" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.918</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.918</annotation></semantics></math>) for normal-versus-malignant detection using the recombined contrast image alone, <math id="S7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.855" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.855</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.855</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.806" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.806</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.806</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.901" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.901</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.901</annotation></semantics></math>) using the low-energy image alone, and <math id="S7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.883" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.883</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.883</annotation></semantics></math>
(<math id="S7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.840" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.840</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.840</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.923" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.923</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.923</annotation></semantics></math>) using both image types together, all under single-image patient fusion and within bootstrap overlap of one another.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Four findings emerge from the analysis. First, the low-energy and recombined contrast images carry statistically indistinguishable malignancy-relevant signal for this feature bank, with no measurable patient-level advantage to either acquisition or to pooling the two; a single image type therefore suffices, and the choice between them can be made on grounds of acquisition cost or dose rather than expected accuracy. Second, the features the classifier selects on the two image types are nearly disjoint and physically interpretable: phase coherence on the low-energy image, where the malignancy signal is geometric, and magnitude distribution on the contrast image, where it is intensity-localized, so the two acquisitions reach equivalent accuracy through different physical channels rather than through redundant information. Third, single-image patient fusion, flagging on the most suspicious image rather than averaging across images, contributes a substantial patient-level lift on the normal-versus-malignant task that holds under a different feature representation as well, large enough that the choice of fusion rule should be reported alongside the
classifier in any multi-image medical classification study. Fourth, under matched patient-grouped evaluation, a pretrained ResNet-50 frozen-feature representation provides no statistically discernible
patient-level advantage over the interpretable wavelet feature bank on either the normal-versus-malignant or the benign-versus-malignant contrast, indicating that the deep representation offers no measurable AUC gain at the clinically relevant level of aggregation while
sacrificing the per-feature physical interpretability that the wavelet representation retains.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The framework matches nonlinear classifiers and a deep-learning feature representation at the patient level on the same patient-grouped folds, while remaining small, fast to train, and interpretable at the level of
individual features. We propose it as a transparent baseline for CESM classification work that follows, including deep-learning pipelines, under matched patient-grouped evaluation.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reproducibility</h5>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All code (<span id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">MATLAB</span> for the feature extraction and classifier pipelines, plus driver scripts for the modality comparison, bootstrap, fusion, classifier comparison, and ResNet-50 frozen-feature analyses) and all per-fold prediction files are available at <a href="https://github.com/saraantonijevic/Masked_Mammograms" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/saraantonijevic/Masked_Mammograms</a>. The CDD-CESM dataset is publicly available from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khaled et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khaled et al., 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
